content.text: Updated March 22, 2026, 5:12 p.m. ETCoverage from the game:Kentucky basketball, Mark Pope must address these things this offseasonWho will be back for UK basketball? An early look at Mark Pope's 2026-27 rosterKentucky basketball season ends with March Madness loss to Iowa StateCoverage during the game:ST. LOUIS — Iowa State's All-American forward, Joshua Jefferson, might take the floor today.He might not.Mark Pope isn't taking any chances."We'll prepare as if he's playing," said Pope, who is in his second season as Kentucky basketball's coach. "You go through this throughout the season where you're kind of prepared for multiple potential opponents. The great thing about Iowa State, and I think what (coach) T.J. (Otzelberger) has done so masterfully at Iowa State, is they have such an engrained identity of who they are."Clearly, Jefferson is a massive key to what they do. Like, he's a special, special player, but Iowa State is going to be Iowa State whoever T.J. rolls out on the court."Jefferson's status is the biggest storyline heading into today's NCAA Tournament game, which is part of the Midwest Region. Kentucky (22-13) is the region's 7-seed; Iowa State (28-7) is No. 2.Watch select 2026 NCAA Tournament games live with Fubo (free trial)The Wildcats are aiming to go 2 for 2 in reaching the Sweet 16 in Pope's tenure, while the Cyclones are seeking their eighth appearance in the round. If ISU wins today, it will mark the first time it's ever advanced to the Big Dance's Sweet 16 in back-to-back seasons.Not if Pope and his players have anything to say about it, though."Our assignment and expectation," he said, "is to win at the highest level every single year — to do everything we can to do that."Courier Journal sports reporter Ryan Black is at the Enterprise Center and will have live updates throughout the game — here and on X, formerly known as Twitter — and complete coverage after.
